data.name: Actual Sunlight
data.detailed_description:
“I know what you’re thinking: Why keep getting up, day in and day out, even though your life is going nowhere?”

Notorious: Widely considered to be one of the bleakest and best-written experiences in indie gaming, Actual Sunlight challenges you to confront the life of Evan Winter: An overweight, lonely and severely depressed young professional.

Fear the words, not the reading: Presented almost entirely in text, a mixture of sharp observation and pitch black humor captures your interest from provocative beginning to shattering conclusion.

Prepare yourself: Actual Sunlight is a uniquely unforgettable adventure that will etch itself into you as one of the most difficult, haunting and beautiful experiences you have ever had as a gamer.

Key Features


  • An intense, heartbreaking story with themes of video game addiction, unsatisfying work and miserable solitude.
  • Beautiful, original pixel and CG artwork invokes the streets, offices and sanctuaries of Toronto, Canada.
  • Dark and moody original music sets a proper tone for the brutal indifference of real life.

Important Notice


Due to explicit language, Actual Sunlight is not appropriate for players under the age of 18.

It also deals with extremely mature themes, including depression and thoughts of suicide. Similar to other forms of art that tackle these issues, Actual Sunlight can be an extremely powerful emotional experience – before downloading it, please first consider what your reaction to a book, film or piece of music in a similar vein might be.

For immediate updates on the game, please follow Will O'Neill on Twitter:

reviews.review:
[b]Trigger Warning: Severe mental health crises and heavy emotional themes.[/b]

[i]I don't have much to say about the mechanics of "Actual Sunlight"—which is because, at its core, the game is a series of texts and raw inner monologues. It doesn't exist to entertain, but to provide a platform for the abysses of the human mind, so I'm going to use it.[/i]

Actual Sunlight is an honest portrait of severe depression and the weight of mental illness that absolutely doesn't pull any punches. It forces you to dive directly into the disturbing thoughts of someone trapped in their own mind. I think way more people should start playing games like this - and especially because of the twisted part that was about "if you feel bad, remember that others have it even worse" made me wanna write a little more uncommon "review":

One of my parents took their life when I was 14, and even though people and aid organizations always say "they didn’t know what they were doing" and "they were out of their mind", I don't believe that. Every case of suicidality I’ve ever encountered was understandable—even if it’s invisible from the outside, the emotional pain leaves an echo that is very often deeply palpable. Sometimes I think that people who think about suicide might be very well in their right mind, and their cognitive dissonance simply stopped working. It is devastatingly hard for those left behind and suicide in the family spreads like a disease that infects everyone differently, yet it is never right to judge someone for taking this step. The pain a family carries after is not comparable to what the person who decided on suicide had to live through.

A few years ago, I assisted in written counseling for a German crisis helpline, specifically for people who find it difficult to talk on the phone due to social anxieties, or for whom it just isn't anonymous enough. Through this, I came to even more understand that endless, all-consuming darkness - but please do not mistake the acute desire for this cruel, paralyzing pain to finally stop with a desire to no longer exist. You don't have to be happy, and you don't have to function or hold up to any expectations and it is okay to do nothing more today than to simply hold on until tomorrow. 

- And what comes tomorrow? Then you hold on through the next day. You don't have to find your way out of the darkness today, or tomorrow, and above all, you do not have to walk alone.
- And what if there is no one? Then it is you who holds on. Even if you feel completely isolated or misunderstood, remember that this pain is not your identity. Your own body, your heart beating away, is fighting for you in every moment. You have already survived every single one of your worst days, so the strength to hold on is already inside you, even if you can't feel it right now. There are people out here who have their own stories and who want you to keep fighting. Love is not always visible, let alone tangible, but it is there—and it believes that you can make it.

I know this sounds like a bad calendar quote about love, hope and happiness you don't wanna hear about, but it is simply how human resilience works. Traumatic survival isn't about feeling good or finding instant hope; it’s about mechanical endurance. About letting the chemical storm in your brain run its course without giving up, because tomorrow your mind will have slightly more space to breathe than it does today.
Crises and traumatic episodes feel permanent, but they are actually like a heavy wave: it builds up, crashes over you, but it will always flatten out again. You don't have to fix your entire life today; you only need to stay alive long enough to begin to see clearly again.

[b]You’re probably here looking for a traditional review to see if this game is worth a buy. And I realize I haven't talked much about the game itself, but I believe games like this exist to make people feel understood and also give a better understanding of a traumatized, suicidal and depressed mindset, so hopefully people will stop judging and start understanding. So yes, it is absolutely worth a buy. Just be prepared to deal with incredibly heavy emotional topics that put you directly into the shoes of someone who has lost all hope.[/b]

A very depressive ending for a review I think. Not sure what to say to make it a little brighter - I guess sparkles and glitter won't do the work here, so maybe a piece of music can give you what words cannot. It's [u][url=https://youtu.be/s_nc1IVoMxc?si=Oa9OU7CHky6V6M5y]a little song[/url][/u] that got pretty popular a few years ago, but carries a lot of raw, unpolished meaning.
